learning: Compare with iteration 1 (0.8 kg, oval finish 0.70, oscillation 0.26) and iteration 4 (0.6 kg, oval finish 0.30, oscillation 0.32). If the oval finish rate is about 0.5 with oscillation at or below 0.3, mass has a monotonic grip effect and 0.7 to 0.8 kg is the usable range. If 0.7 kg matches 0.8 kg, the lower-mass option stays open. If 0.7 kg is worse than 0.6 kg, treat the result as noise and return to 0.8 kg.
notes: Controller held at the iteration 1 values so the race isolates mass 0.7 kg against the 0.8 kg best and the 0.6 kg result. The geometry is the Builder's proposal unchanged.
rationale: Iteration 4 is the only race evidence for mass. At 0.6 kg the oval finish rate fell from 0.70 (iteration 1, 0.8 kg) to 0.30, and oval steering_oscillation rose from 0.26 to 0.32. Iteration 3 showed that a shorter wheel_track (higher yaw gain) also cut oval finishes to 0.10, so yaw gain is not the lever. The Builder's candidate is mass 0.7 kg with the iteration 1 row, 12 mm sensors and wheel_track 0.12 m, which is a single-variable step back toward 0.8 kg. I keep the geometry exactly as proposed. For the controller I reuse the iteration 1 settings (kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.2, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]). Changing the gains as well would confound the mass test, and iteration 4 already showed that the same gains at 0.6 kg lose finishes, so I expect the oval to recover partly and oscillation to sit between 0.26 and 0.32. Because the controller is unchanged, any shift in outcome comes from the mass. The oval finish rate should land near 0.5 if the mass-grip relationship is monotonic. If it does not recover, the next step is mass 0.8 kg, the best known design.
